discover_modules.title: Discover expert parameters
discover_modules.description: Select which modules to search. This opens a short portal session; searching many modules increases the risk of a temporary block (403).

data.refresh: Reload the module list from the portal (rarely needed - the list is cached, and an extra portal login right after the first one can trigger a 403 block)

error.invalid_entityvalue: Invalid entityvalue ID: must be a long hex string (0-9, A-F only; typically 36 characters). Short values like 0 are not a valid ID.
error.invalid_module_arg: Invalid module menu index: digits only (e.g. 6). Leave empty to use the default.
error.duplicate_entityvalue: This parameter is already selected in another slot. Each expert parameter can be used only once.
error.discovery_failed: Could not read from the portal. Try again later (the portal may be temporarily rate-limited).
error.discovery_blocked: Expert access was not attempted: the portal rejected an expert request with 403, so this path is backing off briefly. Sensor polling is unaffected. The exact remaining time and the rejected request are shown at the top of this form. A 403 here does not necessarily mean your IP is rate-limited - it can also mean the portal did not accept that particular request.
error.discovery_empty: The search ran, but the selected module(s) returned no readable parameters. Try another module, or enter the entityvalue manually.
error.discovery_busy: Another expert operation is running for this account right now - a scheduled read, or a value being written. Only one at a time is allowed, so this search was not started. Try again in a moment.
error.invalid_auth: Your stored credentials do not work for the connection this mode uses. The mobile API and the web portal are separate logins, so one of them working says nothing about the other. The mode was not changed.
error.cannot_connect: The connection this mode uses could not be reached, so the mode was not changed. Try again later.
error.rate_limited: The WEM Portal is refusing requests from this network right now, which it does after too many in a short time. The mode was not changed. Waiting is the only fix: it clears by itself, and every retry makes it last longer.

abort.no_changes: No changes to save - the integration was not reloaded.
abort.discovery_aborted: The WEM Portal account this was searching was reloaded or removed, so the search stopped. Nothing was changed. Open the options again once the integration has finished loading.

set_expert_parameter.name: Set expert parameter
set_expert_parameter.description: Writes a Fachmann/expert parameter via the WEM Portal web frontend. Only available while the "Expert write access (web)" option is enabled. The value is validated against the device's own allowed range and the write is verified by re-reading the parameter afterwards. Two limits the service enforces: it only accepts a parameter ID that is configured in one of the ten expert slots, and it refuses when more than one account has expert write enabled - a single service cannot say which account a write is meant for, and guessing would change a setting on the wrong heating system. Requires an administrator: a service call is not covered by the per-user entity permissions Home Assistant applies to the entities themselves.

entityvalue.name: Entity value
entityvalue.description: Hex parameter ID of YOUR installation, taken from the portal's edit dialog URL (entityvalue=...). Installation-specific - do not share publicly.

value.name: Value
value.description: New value. Must be one of the options the device offers.

set_holiday.name: Set holiday
set_holiday.description: Writes the beginning and the end of a holiday in one request. Home Assistant sets one entity at a time, and the portal takes these two parameters only together and only when the range they describe makes sense - a write carrying one of them alone is refused, and a pair whose begin falls after its end is reported as successful and stores nothing. So whichever of the two date entities is set first describes half a range that the portal may discard, which is what this service avoids. Both entities must belong to the same module, and the service refuses a range that ends before it starts rather than reporting a setting that never happened. Requires an administrator: a service call is not covered by the per-user entity permissions Home Assistant applies to the entities themselves.

begin_entity.name: Begin entity
begin_entity.description: The date entity holding the first day of the holiday.

end_entity.name: End entity
end_entity.description: The date entity holding the last day of the holiday. Must belong to the same module as the begin entity - the portal addresses parameters per module.

end.name: End
end.description: Last day of the holiday. Must not be before the begin.
